Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Tuesday gave back a slice of Monday's relief rally, and the AI unwind is now the story. SPY −0.37% and QQQ −0.68%, but NVDA fell 5.47% on 3.11x volume — its second straight heavy down day after Monday's 4.27% on 3.90x — and NBIS −5.27%, COHR −4.68% and BE −4.36% followed it down. iain supplies the warning: failed breakouts, deteriorating leadership and weak rallies into declining MAs “are not the ingredients for new ATHs”, and his four Nov 1 names — MRVL, INTC, ARM, ALAB — are all lower nine days after confirming transitions below their 30-week MA, with bases that “likely need months to rebuild”. Venu supplies the same read from the semiconductor side: former leaders are failing breakouts, losing their 50-day and 200-day moving averages and showing heavy distribution, with many now in declines. Sean supplies the rule that decides the tape: SPY and QQQ are both under the 8/21/50 EMAs, which by his rule means short or sit out — and his $10K-challenge discipline post says wait for the spots, respect the risk, let the account earn bigger size. Remz supplies the other side of the tape: healthcare and biotech “continue to look like the strongest sectors for another leg”, LLY setting up for $1,480–$1,500 with a long trigger over 1,453, and the Q's to watch this week for a reclaim of the key moving averages — plus the AMD bull case, “people trust Lisa and not Jensen”. Enrich supplies the watchlist for today (RKLB, TSLA, BE, AMD, COHR, AMZN) and the NBIS earnings call for Thursday — the 2025 neckline tap at $113 “was generational”, the name is 30%+ off the lows, and he is positioned. Prof supplies the sentiment pivot: CRWV's earnings turned the tape overnight — “Of all the companies that could’ve helped turn sentiment around in AI, I don’t think many expected $CRWV to be the one” — with futures “going absolutely bonkers overnight” (US Tech 100 +1.19% at 21:18 ET), the S&P holding support with 7450 reclaimed and 7650 next if the bottom is in, and a list of 10 names refusing to break down (AMD, AMZN, NET, SPOT, PLTR, SNOW, NVS, OSCR, SPCX, U). DiCarlo supplies the numbers behind the pivot: CRWV revenue $3.66B, up 168% YoY, backlog ~$132B, FY26 guide raised — and the catch, $846M in quarterly interest and ~$47B of debt: “Demand isn't the question. Financing is.” He also flags CIFR as extremely oversold in the Long Term Smart Money Buy Zone, having just tagged out of his short-term position at $9. Your process gives eight genuine qualifiers: LLY (trigger over 1,453, at the high), AAPL (0.62% under its high), AMZN (at the 3-month high), NET (4.10% into the 50-day EMA), NVS (3.18% under its high), U (2.23% under its high), OSCR (+4.14%, above all averages) and MSFT (Venu's 18-month base, trigger $555.28) — plus AMD, PLTR and SNOW holding above the 30-week MA as relative-strength attempts. The decline names tell the other half: NVDA, MRVL, INTC, ARM, ALAB, NBIS, BE and COHR all sit below every average, and CRWV's +6.20% after-hours pop is a sentiment pivot to watch, not a setup — it is still 64.68% under its high. The discipline is in the framing: the qualifiers trigger above, the reclaims trigger above, and Wednesday's follow-through decides whether Prof's overnight turn is real or another weak rally into declining MAs.

  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. LLY's invalidation 1,333 has no anchor nearby, so it shows on its own row; MSFT's trigger $555.28 merges with the 52-week high $555.80; GOOGL's invalidation is the 52-week low 273.50; CIFR's invalidation is the 52-week low 5.55.
